clue.text: Divine inspiration of Pooh's — they go on a ramble

indicators.note: to ramble is to wander about aimlessly, so the letters before it are set wandering into a new order

parts.note: Pooh's is taken with its S as a letter here
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Winnie-the-Pooh fan wonders what inspires the bear and friends as they set off on a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on a ramble' rearranges POOHS plus THEY. The possessive S of Pooh's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical doctrine claiming knowledge of God through direct spiritual insight, a kind of divine illumination.

clue.text: Barnacle said to be so firmly fixed

definitions.meaning: the simile goes 'as ___ as a barnacle', for something clinging fast

explanation.definitionFit: Tight means securely fastened, and a barnacle clinging to a rock is the proverbial image of that grip.

clue.text: A patent wrong — how shocking!

indicators.note: put wrong means set out in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is outraged that a patent has been granted in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges A PATENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Épatant is French for startling or staggering, borrowed for something meant to shock the bourgeois.

clue.text: Heather's in the picture in David's projector in America

indicators.note: in places the heather inside the picture

parts.note: a shot is a photograph
ling is heather; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather appears in a photo with something David projected in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a name; it is the plant LING, its 's giving S. David killed Goliath with a sling; the American name for a catapult is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a catapult for stones is called by this name, and David's weapon against Goliath was such a sling.

clue.text: Poor printer has a little money in joint venture

indicators.note: a poor version is a badly made one, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: p is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: A struggling printer has some cash invested in a shared business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges PRINTER and HAS; P (penny) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership is a business owned and run jointly by two or more people.

clue.text: Blossom on climbing plant here

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: may is hawthorn blossom

explanation.surface: A flower blooms on a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses MAY, the hawthorn's blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: The yam is a tropical climbing vine grown for its starchy tuber.

clue.text: Full Blue grabs the extremities

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it within your grip, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its first and last letters, here of the word the

explanation.surface: An Oxford or Cambridge sporting Blue takes hold of the edges of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabs' puts TE, the first and last letters of 'the' picked out by 'extremities', inside SAD. A Blue is also an Oxbridge sporting honour, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sated has eaten enough to be satisfied, so is full.

clue.text: A formal body

explanation.definitionFit: Stiff describes stilted, starchy manners and is also slang for a corpse.

clue.text: Military band formation adapted to duets

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A marching band's formation is rearranged for pairs of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges TO DUETS. 'band' is a body of soldiers, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The testudo was a Roman army tactic in which soldiers locked shields overhead like a tortoise shell.

clue.text: Thickhead's stupidity

definitions.meaning: split as thick plus head: dense is thick and a ness is a headland, so the word is a thick head

explanation.walkthrough: Ness is a headland (Loch Ness, Sheerness), so 'Thickhead' reads as DENSE + NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dense means being slow-witted, and the noun names that dullness of mind.

clue.text: This artisan is slower when he doesn't use his head

definitions.text: This artisan is slower when he doesn't use his head

parts.words: This artisan is slower when he doesn't use his head
parts.note: take the head letter off the craftsman's name and what is left is a word meaning more idle, that is slower

explanation.surface: A tradesman works more slowly when he does not think.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading the answer leaves LAZIER, which is 'slower'; the clue hints at the window-fitter rather than building him from parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a craftsman who cuts and fits glass in windows.

clue.text: Porcelain manufacturer, the first one in a German city

indicators.note: the first means only the opening letter of the word manufacturer is used
in places the single letter inside the name of the city

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, Germany
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A china maker, the first of its kind, is based in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porcelain manufacturer' reads as a single phrase, but only 'Porcelain' defines; 'the first' takes M from 'manufacturer'. 'in' puts I inside ESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen ware is the fine hard-paste china first made in Europe, named after the Saxon town where it is produced.

clue.text: Sound of a nosy person starting to backbite

indicators.note: starting means just the first letter of the word to is taken

parts.note: read as back plus bite: to bite is to gnaw, and that word written back to front gives these letters

explanation.surface: A busybody begins to speak ill of others behind their backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backbite' splits into 'back' and 'bite': GNAW (bite) turned back gives WANG, after T, the first letter of 'to'. 'nosy' means nasal here, not prying.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of voice, the sound of someone speaking through the nose.

clue.text: You hear this when the hooter blows

definitions.text: You hear this when the hooter blows

parts.words: You hear this when the hooter blows
parts.note: the hooter is slang for the nose, and blowing through it can play a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A factory siren sounds at the end of a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' suggests a siren or car horn; it is slang for the nose, and a nose-blown instrument is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose flute is a pipe instrument played by breath from the nostril, found across the Pacific islands.

clue.text: Flat-finding agency?

parts.note: not a business that finds apartments but a tool that finds when a surface is horizontal, with an alcohol bubble in it

explanation.surface: A letting agent helps you hunt for a flat to rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is level, not an apartment; the bubble sits in alcohol, the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit level is a builder's tool using a bubble in a liquid-filled tube to show that a surface is horizontal.

clue.text: One of the damned, according to Churchill

definitions.text: One of the damned, according to Churchill

parts.words: One of the damned, according to Churchill
parts.note: Churchill grumbled about those damned decimal points in figures, so one of them is a small printed mark

explanation.surface: Winston Churchill names a member of the lost souls in hell.
explanation.walkthrough: As Chancellor, Churchill is said to have complained of 'those damned dots', the decimal points in Treasury figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal point is a small round mark, a spot on the page.

clue.text: Order a sad piper to fade out

indicators.note: order as a verb means arrange, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tells a gloomy bagpiper to slip quietly away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges A SAD PIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to fade from view.

clue.text: Go uphill on skis and get a stitch

definitions.meaning: climbing a slope with ski tips splayed outwards leaves a pattern like a fish skeleton
an embroidery stitch worked in a zigzag like fish bones

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a ski climbing technique with splayed tips and a zigzag sewing stitch, both shaped like a fish skeleton.

clue.text: Receipts which include all standing charges

definitions.text: Receipts which include all standing charges

parts.words: Receipts which include all standing charges
parts.note: not fixed bills but the takings at a ground's entrance, including what standing spectators paid

explanation.surface: An accountant's income includes every fixed fee on a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing charges' suggests the fixed part of a utility bill; here it is the fees paid by spectators who stand on the terraces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gate money is the total takings from admission to a sports ground or show.

clue.text: Queen in miniskirt gets unsympathetic treatment

indicators.note: in places the queen's letter inside the garment

parts.note: a short shift, a shift being a simple straight dress
R, from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch in a miniskirt is treated coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: A miniskirt is read as SHORT SHIFT, a shift being a loose dress; 'in' puts R (Regina) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift is curt, dismissive handling, originally the brief confession allowed to a condemned prisoner.

clue.text: A vent helps the calorific effect

indicators.note: the letters help make up the words that follow, lying within them

explanation.surface: An air vent assists the warming effect of a heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helps' signals the answer sits inside 'calorific effect'.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening, such as a mouth or vent, through which something passes.

clue.text: Idle talk may be natural

definitions.meaning: natural fuel piped into homes from underground

explanation.definitionFit: Gas is both chatter without substance and the fuel found in underground deposits, called natural.

clue.text: Movement Sally heard on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece comes before the river
heard means the word for a joke is spoken and spelt as a near-sound

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a jest
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A girl called Sally is heard moving along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a name but is a quip, JEST; 'heard' gives GEST. 'on' puts it above URE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement of the hand or body made to express meaning.

clue.text: Kind of boy ruler

definitions.meaning: the young male hero of a British pantomime, traditionally played by a woman
a head or chief person, such as the head of a college

explanation.definitionFit: The word means chief or head, and in British Christmas pantomime the leading boy role is called by this name.

clue.text: Sounds like an old woman friend

indicators.note: sounds like means the answer is said like an expression for an old hag

parts.note: a crone is a withered old woman

explanation.surface: Someone's pal resembles an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' points to CRONE with a Y ending, as if crone-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close companion or chum.

clue.text: The prophet's grandma

definitions.meaning: the Hebrew prophet who led the Israelites out of Egypt
Grandma ... was the American folk painter Anna Mary Robertson, who began painting in old age

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to the biblical lawgiver and to an elderly American folk artist always called Grandma.

clue.text: Runner following boat

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow
ff. is the abbreviation for following, as in pages

explanation.surface: A runner pursues a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is a ski, the runner on a sledge or skier.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiff is a small light rowing or sailing boat.

clue.text: Behave theatrically when rebuffed about religious personification

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other
rebuffed, pushed back, means the word for acting is read in reverse

parts.note: to emote is to show feelings in an exaggerated, stagey way
pi is slang for pious, religious

explanation.surface: Someone overacts when snubbed over their spiritual role model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns EMOTE into ETOME; 'about' puts it round PI, crossword slang for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is the perfect embodiment of a quality, the person who personifies it.

clue.text: Decline to go out

explanation.definitionFit: Ebb means to diminish and also names the tide receding from the shore.

clue.text: Italian who invented the Tube

parts.note: not London's Underground but a narrowing pipe used to measure flow, named after an Italian physicist

explanation.surface: An Italian is credited with creating the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is the flow-measuring tube named after the physicist Giovanni Battista Venturi.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Venturi studied fluid flow through a constricted pipe, and the device bears his name.

clue.text: Grassy tracks round Deva's retreat

indicators.note: round means the railway letters go around the other piece

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of tracks

indicators.note: retreat, going back, means the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name of the River Dee and of Chester on it

explanation.surface: Grass-covered paths encircle a hideaway in Roman Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns DEE to EED, and 'round' puts RY around it. Deva was the Roman name for Chester and for its river, the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy describes ground full of reeds, tall grasses of wet land.

clue.text: Tinned meat from first-rate grouse

parts.note: bully is old slang for excellent, as in bully for you
to beef is to complain, to grouse

explanation.surface: A tin of meat comes with an excellent game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb, to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bully beef is corned beef in tins, a staple soldier's ration.
